name: Unconstrained Inputs
essence: Nothing limits how big, how long, or how extreme an input can be — so something downstream pays for it.

examples.summary: A large unit price times four wraps the int64 total.
examples.mechanism: Signed multiplication wraps instead of rejecting a magnitude the domain cannot represent (CWE-190).
examples.expected_behavior: the line rejected, or a total of 12000000000000000000

examples.summary: make is called with a negative length and panics.
examples.mechanism: A length from the caller is not checked before allocation (CWE-400).
examples.observed_output: panic: runtime error: makeslice: len out of range

examples.summary: A label is repeated 8 times with no maximum.
examples.mechanism: strings.Repeat trusts the count, so one request sets the size (CWE-400).

examples.summary: Scaling an untrusted second count into a Duration overflows to a negative timeout.
examples.mechanism: time.Duration is an int64 of nanoseconds; the multiply wraps (CWE-190).

examples.summary: A price times a quantity overflows u32 and panics in a debug build.
examples.mechanism: Debug overflow checks panic; the inputs were never bounded (CWE-190).

examples.summary: A label is repeated 8 times with no maximum.
A second count is cast to u32 and truncated.
examples.mechanism: `as u32` drops the high bits instead of failing the conversion (CWE-190).

examples.summary: A page limit of -1 drops the last row.
examples.mechanism: slice treats a negative end as an offset from the length (CWE-1284).
examples.expected_behavior: the limit rejected, or all four rows

examples.summary: A label is repeated 8 times with no maximum.
A price near the top of the float range times ten prints Infinity.
examples.mechanism: Number multiplication overflows to Infinity instead of rejecting the magnitude (CWE-190).

examples.summary: A group tree four levels deep is counted with no depth cap.
examples.mechanism: The recursion follows every nested list the input contains (CWE-400).
examples.expected_behavior: the tree rejected past the depth cap

examples.summary: A limit of -1 drops dee and returns the first three names.
examples.mechanism: A slice end of -1 counts from the end. It is not rejected as a page size.
examples.expected_behavior: all four names, or a rejected limit

examples.summary: A requested length of 40 is repeated in full.
examples.mechanism: The repeat uses the caller-supplied count. Nothing caps it at a label length.
examples.expected_behavior: a label no longer than 8 characters

examples.summary: The product overflows the float range and becomes inf.
examples.mechanism: Floats overflow to inf instead of failing the multiplication.
examples.expected_behavior: a finite total or a rejected magnitude

examples.summary: A requested depth of 5 is nested in full.
examples.mechanism: Each step wraps another list. The depth argument is not capped.
